examples.ko: 비 오는 날 전기 기구를 만지다가 감전할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got an electric shock when I touched an electrical appliance on a rainy day.
If you touch an outlet with wet hands, you get an electric shock.

examples.ko: 전기 공사 중이던 작업자가 감전해서 병원으로 옮겨졌어요.
examples.en: A worker doing electrical work got shocked and was taken to the hospital.

examples.ko: 어제 형이 감전했는데 다행히 많이 다치지는 않았어요.
examples.en: My older brother got an electric shock yesterday, but luckily he wasn't hurt badly.
To avoid getting shocked, wear rubber gloves while you work.

examples.ko: 아이가 감전하면 큰일이니까 콘센트에 덮개를 씌웠어요.
examples.en: It would be terrible if my child got shocked, so I put covers on the outlets.

explain: '감전 사고'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 가볍게 찌릿한 정도는 '전기가 오르다', '찌릿하다'라고 말해요. '감전되다'도 같은 상황에 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is often used as a noun too, as in '감전 사고' (electric shock accident). For a mild tingle, people say '전기가 오르다' or '찌릿하다'. '감전되다' is also used for the same situation.

examples.en: Your eyes look half-closed, maybe because you're sleepy.
He looked at me with bleary, half-shut eyes.
After staying up all night, my eyes have gone bleary.
He opened his eyes drowsily and got up.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 나서 눈이 거슴츠레하고 졸려요.
examples.en: After taking the medicine, my eyes are heavy and I feel sleepy.

examples.ko: 눈이 거슴츠레해 보이는데 어제 못 잤어요?
examples.en: Your eyes look bleary. Didn't you sleep last night?

explain: 졸리거나 피곤하거나 취해서 눈이 반쯤 감긴 듯 흐릿할 때 쓰는 말이라 '눈'과 함께 가장 많이 써요. '졸리다'처럼 상태를 말하는 것이 아니라 눈 모양과 느낌을 그리는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It is used when the eyes look half-shut and hazy from sleepiness, tiredness or drunkenness, so it pairs mostly with '눈'. Unlike '졸리다', which names a state, it paints how the eyes look.

examples.ko: 누나는 보약을 몇 번이나 먹어도 늘 골골거려요.
examples.en: My sister is always ailing no matter how many tonics she takes.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 골골거려서 병원에 자주 갔어요.
examples.en: I was sickly from childhood, so I often went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 한 달 내내 골골거리고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been feeling under the weather all month because of a cold.

examples.ko: 골골거리지 말고 운동 좀 해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop being sickly all the time and try exercising a bit.

examples.ko: 그 할아버지는 늘 골골거리면서도 오래 사세요.
examples.en: That grandfather is always ailing, yet he lives a long life.
It was cold, so the child kept being unwell.

explain: '골골하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '-거리다'가 붙어서 계속 그러고 있는 모습이 더 느껴져요. 큰 병은 아닌데 자꾸 앓는 사람에게 쓰는 가벼운 구어체라서, 어른에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '골골하다', but the '-거리다' ending makes it feel like the condition keeps going on. It is a light, casual word for someone who is not seriously ill yet keeps ailing, so using it directly about an older person can be rude.

examples.ko: 폭죽 소리가 너무 커서 귀청이 얼얼했어요.
examples.en: The firecrackers were so loud that my ears were ringing.
The baby is crying loud enough to split my ears.
I had my eardrum checked at the hospital for any problems.
Every time a plane passes, I feel it right in my ears.

examples.ko: 공연장 스피커 앞이라 귀청 상할까 봐 귀마개를 썼어요.
examples.en: I was in front of the speakers, so I wore earplugs to protect my ears.

examples.ko: 갑자기 귀청이 터질 듯한 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: Suddenly there was a sound that felt like it would burst my ears.

explain: 의학에서는 '고막'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 소리가 아주 클 때 '귀청이 떨어지다/찢어지다'처럼 과장해서 말해요. 소리가 시끄럽다고 불평할 때 쓰기 좋아요.

phrases.example: 스피커 소리가 커서 귀청이 떨어지는 줄 알았어요.
phrases.en: The speaker was so loud I thought my ears would fall off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 너무 커서 귀가 아플 정도라는 과장 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning a sound is so loud it hurts the ears.

explain_en: In medicine the word is '고막', while in daily talk people exaggerate with '귀청이 떨어지다/찢어지다' when a sound is very loud. It is handy for complaining about noise.

examples.ko: 아버지가 쌀자루를 자전거 꽁무니에 싣고 오셨어요.
examples.en: Dad brought the rice sack on the back of his bicycle.
I followed slowly, watching only the back of the car ahead.
The puppy trails right behind its mother.

examples.ko: 줄 꽁무니는 아직 문 앞에 있었어요.
examples.en: The tail end of the line was still at the door.
A lot of smoke is coming out of the back of the motorcycle.
I can see the end of the train far away.

explain: 자동차, 기차, 줄처럼 움직이는 것의 맨 뒤쪽이나 동물의 꼬리 쪽을 말할 때 써요. '꽁무니를 빼다'는 책임이나 위험한 일에서 슬쩍 물러난다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 일이 어려워지자 친구가 슬그머니 꽁무니를 뺐어요.
phrases.en: When things got hard, my friend quietly backed out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책임지거나 위험한 일에서 몰래 피해 물러날 때 쓰고, 조금 비겁하다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sneaks away from responsibility or danger, with a slightly cowardly feel.

explain_en: It means the very back of something moving, such as a car, a train or a line, or the rear end of an animal. '꽁무니를 빼다' is used for slipping away from responsibility or a risky situation.

examples.ko: 축구를 하다가 머리를 부딪쳐서 뇌진탕 진단을 받았어요.
examples.en: I hit my head playing soccer and was diagnosed with a concussion.

examples.ko: 뇌진탕이 의심되면 바로 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If you suspect a concussion, you have to go to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 넘어진 뒤에 계속 어지러워서 뇌진탕인 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I kept feeling dizzy after I fell, so I thought it was a concussion.

examples.ko: 뇌진탕 때문에 일주일 동안 운동을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested from exercise for a week because of a concussion.

examples.ko: 헬멧을 쓰면 뇌진탕 위험을 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Wearing a helmet can reduce the risk of a concussion.
Luckily, they say it's not a concussion, just a light bruise.

explain: 머리를 세게 부딪친 뒤에 어지럽거나 메스꺼울 때 의심하는 병명이에요. 보통은 '머리를 세게 부딪쳤어요'라고 설명하고, 병원에서 진단을 받으면 이 말을 써요.
explain_en: It is the name of the condition people suspect when they feel dizzy or nauseous after hitting the head hard. Usually people just say they hit their head hard, and this word comes up once a doctor diagnoses it.

examples.en: I fell and broke a rib.
The doctor took an X-ray of the rib area.
My ribs hurt, so it's hard to breathe.

examples.ko: 늑골 골절은 안정을 취하는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: For a rib fracture, resting is important.
I hurt my ribs while exercising and went to the hospital.
The area around my ribs keeps stabbing with pain.

explain: 일상에서는 '갈비뼈'라고 많이 말하고, '늑골'은 병원이나 뉴스, 의학 설명에서 자주 나와요. 고기를 말할 때의 '갈비'와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life people often say '갈비뼈', while '늑골' appears often at hospitals, in the news and in medical explanations. It is different from '갈비', the meat dish.

examples.ko: 감기에 된통 걸려서 일주일 동안 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I caught a terrible cold and lay in bed for a week.
I got a real scolding from my manager yesterday.
I started a business and got burned badly.
I slipped on the ice and landed hard on my backside.
I got caught badly by my mom while lying.
I fell on the street and got badly hurt.

explain: '몹시, 심하게'라는 느낌이지만 주로 감기에 걸리다, 혼나다, 당하다처럼 나쁜 일에 써요. '아주'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '된통'은 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고, 편한 대화에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of 'badly, severely' and is mostly used with bad things such as catching a cold, being scolded or getting burned. Unlike the all-purpose '아주', '된통' is not used for good things and is common in casual conversation.

examples.en: I ate shrimp and broke out in hives all over.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 두드러기가 심해져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My hives got worse after taking the medicine, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 두드러기가 나면 가려워서 자꾸 긁게 돼요.
examples.en: When you get hives, it itches and you keep scratching.
I'm worried because hives have come up on my child's arm.
Hives sometimes go away after a few days.

examples.ko: 꽃가루 때문에 두드러기가 생기는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people get hives from pollen.

explain: 음식이나 약, 꽃가루 같은 알레르기 때문에 피부가 붉게 부풀고 가려운 증상이에요. '두드러기가 나다/생기다/올라오다'처럼 쓰고, 소리가 비슷한 '두드러지다'(눈에 띄다)와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is a red, swollen, itchy skin reaction, often caused by allergies to food, medicine or pollen. It is used as '두드러기가 나다/생기다/올라오다', and don't confuse it with the similar-sounding '두드러지다' (to stand out).

examples.en: My father is sleeping, snoring loudly.

examples.ko: 옆자리 승객이 드르렁 코를 골아서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The passenger next to me snored loudly, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 동생이 눕자마자 드르렁 소리를 내며 잠들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling fell asleep with a loud snore as soon as he lay down.

examples.ko: 드르렁 하는 소리에 놀라서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up startled by a loud snoring sound.
My husband snores loudly all night.

examples.ko: 강아지도 드르렁 하고 코를 골며 자요.
examples.en: Even the puppy sleeps snoring loudly.

explain: 크게 코 고는 소리를 나타내요. 보통 '드르렁드르렁'으로 반복해서 많이 말하고, '코를 골다'와 같이 써요. 문이 열리는 소리 '드르륵'과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of loud snoring. It is most often repeated as '드르렁드르렁' and used together with '코를 골다'. Don't confuse it with '드르륵', the sound of a door sliding open.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 따귀를 맞는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in the movie where the main character gets slapped in the face.

examples.ko: 화가 난 형이 동생에게 따귀부터 올려붙였어요.
examples.en: The angry older brother slapped his younger brother across the face first.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 따귀 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The sound of the slap in the drama was so loud that I was startled.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 거짓말을 해서 따귀를 맞은 적이 있대요.
examples.en: I heard that when he was little he got slapped for lying.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 따귀를 맞은 것처럼 얼굴이 화끈거렸어요.
examples.en: After hearing those words, my face burned as if I had been slapped.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 사람의 따귀를 때리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, you must not slap someone's face.

explain: '뺨'을 조금 속되게 부르는 말이라서 주로 '따귀를 때리다', '따귀를 맞다'처럼 맞는 장면에서 써요. 얼굴 부위를 말할 때는 '뺨'이나 '볼'을 쓰고, '따귀'는 그런 뜻으로 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: This is a somewhat rough word for '뺨' (cheek), and it is mostly used in set phrases like '따귀를 때리다' and '따귀를 맞다' for slapping. To talk about the part of the face, use '뺨' or '볼' instead.

examples.en: The child started crying at the top of its lungs.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 타고난 목청 덕분에 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That singer is popular thanks to a naturally powerful voice.
He is tall and has a booming voice too.
I cleared my throat and began the presentation.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 목청은 큰데 마음은 여려요.
examples.en: My father has a loud voice, but he's tender-hearted.

examples.ko: 그는 목청 높여 자기 의견을 말했어요.
examples.en: He raised his voice and gave his opinion.

explain: '목소리'와 달리 소리를 내는 힘이나 크기에 초점이 있어요. '목청이 좋다/크다', '목청을 높이다/가다듬다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '목소리' (voice), 목청 focuses on the power and volume of the voice. It is used in '목청이 좋다/크다' and '목청을 높이다/가다듬다'.

en: be sick in bed; be laid up

examples.en: My cold was so bad that I was laid up for two days.
My grandmother fell ill and took to her bed, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 과로로 몸져누운 동료 대신 제가 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked in place of a colleague who was laid up from overwork.

examples.ko: 몸져눕기 전에 미리 쉬는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to rest in advance before you end up in bed sick.
I've been in bed sick for a few days, so I have no appetite.
I was sick enough to be bedridden, but nobody knew.

explain: 병이 심해서 자리에 누워 일어나지 못할 때 써요. 그냥 '아파서 눕다'보다 한동안 앓는 느낌이 있어요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '몸져누워요'가 되고, 높임은 '몸져누우시다'예요.
explain_en: It means being so ill that you lie down and cannot get up. It feels more like being sick in bed for a while than simply lying down because you're unwell. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb ('몸져누워요'), and the honorific is '몸져누우시다'.

en: sheet of paper; pale as a sheet

examples.en: His face turned white as a sheet.

examples.ko: 무서운 소식을 듣고 그의 얼굴이 백지장이 됐어요.
examples.en: After hearing the frightening news, his face went pale.

examples.ko: 백지장도 맞들면 낫다고 같이 하면 훨씬 쉬워요.
examples.en: As they say, many hands make light work, so it's much easier together.
Your face looks pale as paper, are you sick?
In the cold weather, her lips turned white as paper.

examples.ko: 백지장 같던 얼굴에 조금씩 핏기가 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: Little by little, color returned to his paper-white face.

explain: 종이처럼 하얗게 질린 얼굴빛을 말할 때 '얼굴이 백지장 같다, 백지장처럼 하얗다'로 써요. 놀람, 아픔, 추위 때문에 핏기가 없을 때 어울려요.

phrases.example: 이삿짐이 많으니까 백지장도 맞들면 낫다고 같이 옮겨요.
phrases.en: Even a sheet of paper is lighter when two people lift it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 쉬운 일도 함께 하면 더 낫다는 속담이에요. 도움을 청하거나 같이 하자고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even an easy task goes better when done together. Used when asking for help or suggesting you do it together.

explain_en: It describes a face drained of color, as in '얼굴이 백지장 같다' or '백지장처럼 하얗다'. It fits when someone looks bloodless from shock, illness or cold.

examples.en: I caught a cold and was dragging around weakly all day.
Why are you so listless? Have you eaten?
Stop being so feeble and do some exercise.
I worked late yesterday, so I came in walking limply from this morning.
The child seems to have a fever and is listless.
I gave plenty of water to the wilting plant.

explain: 몸이 약하거나 아파서 힘없이 흐느적거릴 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 약간 놀리는 느낌이 될 수 있고, 식물이 시들시들할 때도 말해요. 부사 '비실비실'과 짝이 되는 동사예요.
explain_en: It is used when someone is weak or sick and moves around without energy. Said to a person it can sound a bit teasing, and it can also describe a wilting plant. It is the verb that pairs with the adverb '비실비실'.

examples.en: After lunch, drowsiness hits me.

examples.ko: 식곤증 때문에 오후 회의 내내 졸았어요.
examples.en: I dozed through the whole afternoon meeting because of post-meal sleepiness.
I drank coffee to shake off my after-lunch sleepiness.
For post-meal sleepiness, a light walk is good.

examples.ko: 식곤증과 싸우는 오후 두 시가 제일 힘들어요.
examples.en: Two in the afternoon, when I fight post-meal drowsiness, is the hardest.
Anyone can get sleepy after a meal.

explain: 밥을 먹은 뒤에 나른하고 졸린 것을 말해요. '식곤증이 오다', '식곤증이 몰려오다'처럼 써요. 봄에 나른하고 졸린 '춘곤증'과 짝으로 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It means feeling sluggish and sleepy after eating. You say '식곤증이 오다' or '식곤증이 몰려오다'. It is worth learning alongside '춘곤증', the springtime sluggishness.

examples.ko: 신짝 한 짝이 어디 갔는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know where one of my shoes went.
The puppy ran off with my shoe in its mouth.

examples.ko: 아이 신짝은 현관에 아무렇게나 널려 있어요.
examples.en: The child's shoes are scattered all over the entrance.
The shoes are so worn out that I need to buy new ones.
I ran out in a hurry without even grabbing my shoes.
The shoes are covered with dirt.

explain: 신발 이야기를 할 때는 보통 '신발'이나 '신'이라고 하고, '신짝'은 한 짝을 말할 때나 '헌신짝'이라는 표현에서 주로 나와요. 가볍거나 조금 거친 말투에 어울려요.

phrases.en: He threw away his old friend like a worn-out shoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요할 때는 쓰다가 쓸모가 없어지면 아무 미련 없이 버린다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a critical tone: using someone or something when needed and discarding it without regret once it is useless.
phrases.en_equiv: toss aside like an old shoe

explain_en: For shoes in general people usually say '신발' or '신', while '신짝' mainly appears when talking about a single shoe or in the expression '헌신짝'. It fits a light or slightly rough tone.

examples.en: I hurt my ankle ligament playing soccer.
My ligament was stretched, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 무릎 인대를 다치지 않게 운동 전에 준비운동을 해요.
examples.en: I warm up before exercise so I don't hurt my knee ligaments.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 인대 검사를 해 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said we should do a ligament test.
People with weak ligaments often sprain things.

examples.ko: 수술 뒤에 인대가 붙을 때까지 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: After surgery, you have to rest until the ligament heals.

explain: 뼈와 뼈를 이어 주는 질긴 조직이고, 발목이나 무릎을 다쳤다는 말에서 자주 들어요. '근육'은 움직이게 하는 부분, '인대'는 관절을 붙잡아 주는 부분이에요. 보통 '인대가 늘어나다', '인대가 끊어지다'로 써요.
explain_en: A ligament connects bone to bone, and you mostly hear the word when someone hurts an ankle or knee. 근육 (muscle) moves the body, while 인대 holds the joint in place. Typical verbs are 늘어나다 (stretch) and 끊어지다 (tear).

examples.en: I seem to be coming down with a cold, since I have a slight cough.
A little cough keeps me from sleeping well every night.
He came into the room with a small cough.
Even a light cough, if it continues, should be checked at a hospital.
I keep hearing small coughs from the next seat.
The light cough lasted a long time, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 크게 콜록거리는 기침이 아니라 작고 자주 나오는 기침이에요. '헛기침'은 목을 가다듬거나 신호로 일부러 하는 기침이고, 잔기침은 자꾸 나오는 작은 기침에 주로 써요.
explain_en: It is a small, frequent cough rather than a big hacking one. '헛기침' is a cough you make on purpose to clear your throat or give a signal, while '잔기침' mostly refers to small coughs that keep coming.

examples.en: My sleeve got caught on a nail and ripped.

examples.ko: 봉지가 무거운 짐 때문에 째져 버렸어요.
examples.en: The bag split because of the heavy load.
Jeans ripped at the knees are in style these days.
My pants suddenly ripped, and I was so embarrassed.

examples.ko: 눈이 위로 째진 고양이가 창가에 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A cat with upturned eyes is sitting by the window.

examples.ko: 찢어진 데가 더 째지지 않게 테이프를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put tape on it so the tear wouldn't split further.

explain: '찢어지다'와 비슷하지만 틈이 길게 벌어지는 느낌이 있어요. '찢어지다'가 더 널리 쓰이고, 눈 모양을 말할 때는 '눈이 째지다', '째진 눈'이라고 해요. 눈 얘기는 외모 평가가 되기 쉬우니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 우리 집은 째지게 가난했어요.
phrases.en: When I was young, our family was dirt poor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '째지다'의 본뜻과 달리 '몹시, 지독하게'라는 뜻으로 가난을 강조해요. 대화체에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the original meaning of '째지다', it works as 'terribly' to emphasize poverty. It is used in conversation.

explain_en: It is similar to '찢어지다' but has a feel of a long gap opening up. '찢어지다' is more widely used, and for eye shape people say '눈이 째지다' or '째진 눈'. Talking about eyes can sound like judging someone's looks, so be careful.

examples.en: I have a cold, so my voice sounds nasal.
That singer adds a nasal tone when singing.
The child acts cute in a nasal voice.

examples.ko: 콧소리 때문에 말이 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The nasal sound makes it hard to hear what you say.
My nose is blocked, so I end up talking through my nose.
Don't talk through your nose; speak clearly.

explain: 코가 막혔을 때 '콧소리가 나다'라고 해요. 일부러 코로 내는 귀여운 목소리는 '콧소리를 내다'라고 하는데, 애교를 부릴 때 많이 써요. 코가 막힌 목소리는 '코맹맹이 소리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: When your nose is blocked, you say '콧소리가 나다'. A cute voice made through the nose on purpose is '콧소리를 내다', often used when acting charming. A blocked-nose voice is also called '코맹맹이 소리'.

examples.en: My friend who climbed the hill spoke while panting.
Why are you panting like that?
Even while gasping, I ran to the end.

examples.ko: 조금만 걸어도 헉헉거리면 운동을 시작해야 해요.
examples.en: If you pant after a short walk, you need to start exercising.
I was huffing and puffing, but I didn't give up until the finish line.

examples.ko: 헉헉거리지 말고 천천히 숨을 쉬어 봐요.
examples.en: Stop gasping and try breathing slowly.

explain: '헉헉대다'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 달리기나 계단을 오른 뒤 숨이 차서 힘든 모습에 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 강아지처럼 숨을 거칠게 쉬는 동물에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '헉헉대다'. It is used for being out of breath and struggling after running or climbing stairs. It can be used not only for people but also for animals breathing hard, like dogs.

examples.ko: 언덕을 오르자 아이가 헐떡헐떡 숨을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: After climbing the hill, the child breathed heavily, panting.

examples.ko: 헐떡헐떡 뛰어온 걸 보니 많이 급했나 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you run over panting, you must have been in a big hurry.

examples.ko: 강아지가 혀를 내밀고 헐떡헐떡 숨을 몰아쉬어요.
examples.en: The puppy sticks out its tongue and pants hard.

examples.ko: 그는 헐떡헐떡 거친 숨을 내쉬며 의자에 앉았어요.
examples.en: He sat down on the chair, letting out rough, panting breaths.

examples.ko: 마라톤을 마친 선수가 헐떡헐떡 바닥에 주저앉았어요.
examples.en: The runner who finished the marathon collapsed on the ground, gasping.

examples.ko: 환자가 헐떡헐떡 힘들게 숨을 쉬어서 걱정돼요.
examples.en: The patient is breathing with difficulty, gasping, and I'm worried.

explain: 숨이 가쁘게 자꾸 쉬는 소리나 모습을 흉내 낸 말이라서 '숨을 쉬다', '뛰어오다' 같은 말 앞에 와요. 같은 모습을 '숨을 헐떡이다'처럼 동사로도 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the look and sound of fast, labored breathing, so it comes before words like '숨을 쉬다' or '뛰어오다'. The same scene can be said with the verb in '숨을 헐떡이다'.
